input.quote: 14.2.2 At-Will Termination by PB. PB may terminate this Agreement at any time after SFJ has paid or incurred a total of $60 million of Development Costs and prior to the date of receipt of the first Regulatory Approval upon [***] prior written notice to SFJ.
input.rationale: Section 14.2.2 is PB's only at-will exit and it fails the fallback on material terms: it does not open until SFJ has paid or incurred $60 million of Development Costs, it closes entirely on receipt of the first Regulatory Approval, and the notice figure is left blank ([***]) rather than set within the 60-90 day band. In a multi-year development term that is not a usable customer convenience right. The single replace restores an express grant - "PB may terminate this Agreement for convenience, without cause, at any time upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to SFJ" - adds a pro rata refund of PB's prepayments (broadened from "fees" because this Agreement has no defined fee concept and uses Development Costs, Approval Payments and the Buy-Out Payment; the limb is harmless if nothing is prepaid), and states that SFJ has no convenience termination right during the Term. SFJ's exits (14.2.3 MAE, 14.2.5 bankruptcy, 14.2.6 Change of Control, 14.2.7 safety, 14.2.8.1 compliance breach, 14.2.9 Adverse Patent Impact, 14.2.10 JSC decision) are trigger-conditioned rather than at-will, so we do not flag them as vendor convenience rights and they do not contradict the new sentence. We target preferred because the fallback's three-months-of-fees cap has no analogue here: the retained 300% Development Cost amount is consideration for purchasing the Trial Data Package under Section 11.1.1.4 and is left untouched, as is the ARTICLE 6 carry-over. Noted commercially rather than redlined: the exit is unconditional but not free (300% plus continuing Approval Payments), and 14.2.10 is close to discretionary in practice.

proposal.summary: Make PB's termination right an unconditional convenience exit on 30 days' written notice with pro rata refund of prepayments, and bar SFJ convenience termination during the Term.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We need a clear, unconditional customer exit: as drafted PB's at-will right only opens after SFJ has spent $60 million, closes at first Regulatory Approval, and leaves the notice period blank. We have made it an express termination for convenience without cause on thirty (30) days' written notice with a pro rata refund of any PB prepayments, and confirmed SFJ has no convenience termination right during the Term; we have left the 300% Development Cost payment for the Trial Data Package intact, so please note this exit remains costly and we may revert to that pricing separately.

ops.oldText: PB may terminate this Agreement at any time after SFJ has paid or incurred a total of $60 million of Development Costs and prior to the date of receipt of the first Regulatory Approval upon [***] prior written notice to SFJ.
ops.newText: PB may terminate this Agreement for convenience, without cause, at any time upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to SFJ, and SFJ will refund pro rata any fees or other amounts prepaid by PB for the period after the effective date of termination. SFJ has no right to terminate this Agreement for convenience during the Term.

mappings.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
